c.tagline: Germany's oldest city, built on 2,000 years of Roman stone.

taxi.fareNote: Cream-colored taxis wait at ranks near the Hauptbahnhof and Porta Nigra and run on regulated meters; the FreeNow app is commonly used for booking.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 112 reaches fire and medical services; both work nationwide in Germany.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: Home to the Roman Porta Nigra gate, Trier Cathedral, and the bustling Hauptmarkt, this compact core packs two millennia of history into a few walkable blocks. Cafés and shops line pedestrian streets radiating from the market square. It's the obvious base for sightseeing.

The area around the Hauptbahnhof and the Kaiserthermen Roman baths, mixing transit convenience with Roman ruins. Ostallee and nearby streets offer everyday shopping and dining. It's a practical, well-connected base just south of the historic center.

A picturesque former fishing quarter along the Moselle riverbank, lined with pastel-colored houses and a relaxed promenade. It's quieter than the Altstadt but only a short stroll away. Riverside cafés make it a pleasant spot for an evening walk.

Home to the University of Trier's city campus, this hillside district has a young, casual energy with student bars and affordable eateries. It sits above the Altstadt with views over the city. Nightlife here skews toward students rather than tourists.

A quiet residential district on the west bank of the Moselle, reached via the ancient Roman Bridge. It offers a slower pace, with local vineyards climbing the hillside behind it. Few tourists venture here, making it a peaceful overnight base.

landmarks: Porta Nigra
The blackened Roman city gate of 170 AD, mightiest north of the Alps, still towers over Trier as the UNESCO-listed emblem of Germany's oldest city.
Trier Cathedral (Dom St. Peter)
Germany's oldest cathedral, begun under Constantine, layers Roman, Romanesque and Baroque grandeur and enshrines the Holy Robe relic attributed to Christ.
Liebfrauenkirche (Church of Our Lady)
Adjoining the cathedral, this 13th-century church ranks among Germany's earliest Gothic buildings, its cruciform rose-plan interior glowing with vivid modern glass.
Konstantin-Basilika (Aula Palatina)
Constantine's colossal brick throne hall, the largest surviving single-room structure of antiquity, humbles visitors with its 33-metre-high unsupported ceiling.
Kaiserthermen (Imperial Baths)
Wander the soaring ruined walls and eerie underground service tunnels of one of the Roman Empire's grandest bathing complexes, begun around 300 AD.
Roman Amphitheatre
Gladiators once battled before 20,000 spectators in this hillside arena among vineyards; descend into the cellar where beasts and fighters awaited their fate.
Hauptmarkt
One of Germany's loveliest market squares gathers a medieval market cross, Renaissance fountain and gabled townhouses beneath the Gothic spire of St. Gangolf.
Karl Marx House
The Baroque townhouse where Marx was born in 1818 is now a thoughtful museum tracing his life, work and world-changing ideas.
Electoral Palace and Gardens
A pink-and-gold Rococo palace facade, counted among the world's most beautiful, opens onto formal gardens beside Constantine's basilica, framing perfect photographs.
Römerbrücke (Roman Bridge)
Still carrying traffic across the Moselle on 2nd-century basalt piers, this is Germany's oldest bridge and a quietly astonishing feat of Roman engineering.

train.note: Trier has a genuine cross-border commuter link: regional trains run to Luxembourg City in about 50 minutes, and once you are over the border all public transport in Luxembourg is free. Domestically, trains follow the Moselle to Koblenz in 1h30 and reach Saarbrücken in an hour; for Cologne you change at Koblenz. DB Sparpreis fares open six months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches use the stop beside the Hauptbahnhof. Trier sits close to both the Luxembourg and Belgian borders, so regional cross-border buses supplement the trains - the RGTR network into Luxembourg is free once across. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. The Moselle carries river-cruise ships and summer excursion boats between Trier and Bernkastel-Kues, which are sightseeing trips rather than transport.

half.name: Bernkastel-Kues
half.blurb: Bernkastel-Kues is a half-timbered wine town on the Moselle River surrounded by steep vineyard slopes.

half.name: Luxembourg
half.blurb: Luxembourg City sits across the border with fortified ramparts, deep gorges and a UNESCO-listed old quarter.

half.name: Saarburg
half.blurb: Saarburg has a waterfall running through the middle of its old town on the Saar River, near vineyard terraces.

half.name: Cochem
half.blurb: Cochem is a Moselle River town below a restored hilltop castle, with a compact half-timbered old center.
